summary: Weekly POC sync to review quality eval results from the last sprint. Discussed prompt-set performance, regression signals, guardrail tuning, and next steps for dedicated pilot and additional telemetry. Action items assigned for running more constrained regression tests and sharing failing examples.
transcript:
Header: 2025-07-15 10:00 PDT | Duration: 45 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Jordan Miller (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Ravi Kumar (Redwood CSM), Carlos Rivera (FinSight Head of Data), Maya Chen (FinSight ML Eng), Liam O'Neill (FinSight PM)

00:00:03 - Jordan Miller: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, we got like 45 minutes on the calendar, quick introc, Samira's gonna run through the quality eval we did this week.
00:00:12 - Carlos Rivera: yeah thanks Jordan, appreciate it, we've been looking forward to this.
00:00:18 - Samira Patel: cool hi team, I'll share my screen in a second, um quick agenda - results, top failing prompts, suggested prompt changes, regression thresholds, and next steps.
00:00:30 - Maya Chen: quick note, we pushed 800 new test cases last night, a mix of short-form Q/A and long context doc summarization.
00:00:40 - Samira Patel: perfect that helps. ok first slide, overall pass rate across the prompt set is about 82% for the current Redwood hosted model variant, and about 85% on the larger config but with 1.8x latency. we saw a small drop on exact-match metrics for the billing-related prompts.
00:00:57 - Liam O'Neill: when you say pass rate, can you remind us how that's computed?
00:01:02 - Samira Patel: yeah sorry, pass rate is our acceptance heuristic - exact match for canonical answers when available, otherwise rubric-based accept/reject from the eval sheet. so it's a mix, we also have a human-verified subset.
00:01:18 - Carlos Rivera: ok, that's fine, we care most about the billing questions and hallucinations on invoice numbers. those are showstoppers.
00:01:26 - Samira Patel: understood. slide 2 shows the top 12 failing prompts, 7 of them are billing, 3 are entity resolution where the model pulls wrong vendor names, and 2 are long-doc summarization where the model drops a policy clause.
00:01:40 - 00:02:05 - Speaker 1: (mumble) the transcription here might not be 100% but gist is we have the failing list in the sheet - link pasted in the chat - https://drive.google.com/fin_sight_eval
00:02:12 - Maya Chen: we see also higher false positives on the guardrail classifier on tone detection, it flags some legitimate content as risky.
00:02:20 - Samira Patel: yeah that's likely due to the classifier threshold. I recommend lowering the sensitivity for our guardrail on those merchant names, and add a white-list for known vendors.
00:02:29 - Carlos Rivera: white-listing is fine but we need auditable justification for any whitelist. security asks for a change log.
00:02:36 - Jordan Miller: we can capture that in the audit log, Redwood's Private and Dedicated have configurable audit trails - we'll include the change reason tied to the policy change.
00:02:45 - Liam O'Neill: question on latency: the larger config had better quality but double the token time, how feasible is it to get the same quality with quantized weights or batching tweaks?
00:02:57 - Samira Patel: good question - quantization can offer 1.5-2x throughput improvements with slight quality loss. we tested an int8 profile on a subset and saw a 1.1% drop on exact match, so probably acceptable for non-billing prompts but not for invoice extraction.
00:03:15 - Maya Chen: so for billing we should keep the fp16 config?
00:03:18 - Samira Patel: yes that's my recommendation. for everything else we can push a cheaper quantized variant.
00:03:24 - 00:03:45 - Speaker 2: (overlap) also we noted some flakiness in the hosted environment during peak that might be rate-limit related, that impacted a couple of regression runs.
00:03:48 - Jordan Miller: thanks for calling that out - we saw a transient spike at 03:12 UTC yesterday due to a concurrent benchmark job. we've applied a soft rate limit and are re-running the affected evals.
00:03:59 - Carlos Rivera: can you log that as an incident? we need it for our procurement review.
00:04:04 - Ravi Kumar: I'll open an incident in the tracker and attach the logs and timeline.
00:04:10 - Samira Patel: moving on, I want to show an example failing case - prompt #034 billing_invoices_count where the model returns a sum that doesn't match the invoice table.
00:04:20 - 00:04:50 - Samira Patel: (reads) input: 'How many invoices in March for vendor X exceed $5,000?' expected: '3' model output: '4; vendor Y included' so we see entity resolution leaking in.
00:04:56 - Maya Chen: is that from a context window overflow or wrong table parsing?
00:05:02 - Samira Patel: appears to be table-parsing error; the model concatenated rows from a neighboring vendor row when the CSV had inconsistent delimiters. we've flagged this and added a guard in the prompt to enforce delimiter normalization.
00:05:18 - Carlos Rivera: can Redwood preprocess those tables as part of the pipeline?
00:05:22 - Jordan Miller: yes we can add a preprocessing step in the route - normalizing CSV/TSV - small config change. it's part of the Dedicated/private pipeline as well if you want it isolated.
00:05:30 - Liam O'Neill: about regression detection thresholds - right now you said the alert fires at a 5% drop in pass rate?
00:05:36 - Samira Patel: correct. we configured an initial threshold of 5% on weekly rolling average. we can add more granular per-prompt thresholds; for billing prompts we recommended 1.5% to catch small but critical regressions.
00:05:48 - Maya Chen: would that increase noise? we get a lot of variance on smaller prompt samples.
00:05:53 - Samira Patel: yes sample size matters. recommendation: per-prompt thresholds plus a minimum sample size (we used 30 examples) and a smoothing window of 7 days to reduce churn.
00:06:05 - Carlos Rivera: that sounds reasonable. can Redwood send the alert config as YAML we can import?
00:06:10 - Jordan Miller: yes we'll share the alert config and a suggested per-prompt policy in the repo.
00:06:15 - 00:06:45 - Speaker 3: (background) also asked about rollback automation if a rollout causes a regression, like auto-revert to the previous model variant.
00:06:47 - Samira Patel: we support automatic rollback in Dedicated and private, and hosted we have a canary policy that will automatically fallback to the last known good model if a safety/regression alert trips. we can configure the sensitivity.
00:06:59 - Maya Chen: would that also switch region if capacity is an issue?
00:07:03 - Samira Patel: we have smart routing policies - you can route by latency, cost, or region and use fallback variants. cross-region fallback is possible but watch out for data residency.
00:07:13 - Carlos Rivera: data residency is a blocker for some of our customers in EU, we'll need VPC/private deployment for those.
00:07:18 - Jordan Miller: noted, that's exactly where Redwood Private fits. we can package an on-prem agent or VPC connector.
00:07:24 - 00:07:50 - Samira Patel: next I want to show the regression chart - you can see the spike on 07/12 where pass rate dipped 6% mostly driven by 3 billing prompts. after re-tuning the prompt and adding a vendor whitelist we recovered to within 1% by 07/14.
00:07:56 - Maya Chen: did you run a confusion matrix on the classifier? we want to see false positives vs false negatives.
00:08:02 - Samira Patel: yes attached in the sheet - false positive rate for tone classifier is 8% on this sample, and false negative is 3%. adjusting threshold would trade those off.
00:08:12 - Liam O'Neill: curious about cost modelling: can you show delta in token costs between the fp16 and int8 runs?
00:08:19 - Samira Patel: on the sample workload fp16 run cost was $0.012 per 1k tokens, int8 was $0.007 per 1k tokens - rough numbers; depends on throughput and reserved capacity.
00:08:32 - Carlos Rivera: those numbers help; if we do a dedicated pilot we can probably negotiate better units.
00:08:36 - Jordan Miller: yes dedicated reserved capacity gives predictable unit economics, we can lay out a 3-week pilot with burn rate and KPIs.
00:08:44 - 00:09:10 - Speaker 4: (crosstalk) we also ran an adversarial prompt set to test guardrails, about 120 prompts, the model failed safe on about 95% which is good but we got a few edge cases where it produced partial disclosures.
00:09:17 - Samira Patel: for disclosures we can tighten the guardrail policy and add post-processing redaction step for PII patterns. that reduced leakage on our test to 0.4% in prior pilots.
00:09:27 - Maya Chen: can you point to the post-processing regex or is it baked into the runtime?
00:09:30 - Samira Patel: it's a pipeline step that can be configured in the route. we'll share the regex patterns we used; they are customizable.
00:09:36 - Carlos Rivera: are those patterns auditable? security will want to review them.
00:09:39 - Jordan Miller: yes we keep change logs and version the guardrail rules; Private customers can run their own patterns too.
00:09:45 - 00:10:10 - Samira Patel: quick note on scoring methodology - we used exact-match where possible, otherwise an annotator rubric. we also compute a semantic similarity score for free-form answers using embedding distance as a fallback. this helps surface near-misses.
00:10:23 - Liam O'Neill: what's the threshold for semantic similarity considered acceptable?
00:10:27 - Samira Patel: we used cosine similarity > 0.78 on the evaluation embed model; above that we mark as a near-match and flag for human review.
00:10:36 - Maya Chen: can we tune that per prompt type?
00:10:38 - Samira Patel: yes per prompt tuning is supported. we can also store labeled examples to retrain the thresholding model.
00:10:46 - 00:11:05 - Speaker 1: (murmur) someone asked about the eval sheet columns, like "context_length" and "kv_cache_hit" - want to keep that for debugging.
00:11:12 - Samira Patel: we included those columns - context length, kv cache hit, latency_ms, token_count, model_variant - all helpful for triage.
00:11:20 - Carlos Rivera: are kv cache hits improving average latency for our summary flows?
00:11:24 - Samira Patel: yes about 15% latency improvement when KV hits are high for multi-turn flows, so it's worthwhile to enable caching for repeat prefixes.
00:11:33 - Maya Chen: ok on action items - we will extract failing examples and redact PII then upload.
00:11:38 - Samira Patel: perfect, once we have the failing examples we can run focused retraining or do prompt engineering and re-run the eval.
00:11:46 - Jordan Miller: moving to risks - Carlos you mentioned procurement needs. anything else?
00:11:51 - Carlos Rivera: SOC 2 and ISO are table stakes; can you share your latest SOC 2 report and pen-test summary?
00:11:58 - Jordan Miller: yes will send SOC 2 Type II and our pen-test executive summary. also will include the data retention and KMS docs.
00:12:07 - Maya Chen: one more technical Q - on inconsistency between runs, do you persist RNG seeds or is there nondeterminism?
00:12:13 - Samira Patel: we expose a seed param for deterministic decoding on a given model variant, but production sampling may still vary due to temperature and streaming tokens; for eval we lock the seed.
00:12:24 - 00:12:54 - Speaker 2: (stutter) unexpected - the customer asked if Redwood could run a head-to-head benchmark against OpenAI on the same prompt set, including latency from their region.
00:12:58 - Jordan Miller: we can run a head-to-head; need permission for API keys and the terms. also note differences in tokenization and model behavior - we'll normalize best we can.
00:13:09 - Carlos Rivera: yes please run it, include p50/p95 latency and exact match and hallucination rate.
00:13:16 - Samira Patel: noted, we'll run that and share a comparison sheet.
00:13:20 - 00:13:45 - Samira Patel: quick demo of a prompt tweak: original prompt used 'Count invoices' with loose spec, updated prompt adds 'Only count unique invoice_id and ignore vendor Y', this fixed the entity bleed in our test.
00:13:50 - Maya Chen: can we automate those prompt masks based on known vendor list?
00:13:55 - Samira Patel: yes you can include a prefilled variable list in the prompt pipeline; Redwood routes support parameterized templates.
00:14:02 - Liam O'Neill: on scoring regressions, would you recommend alerting on absolute drop or relative percent?
00:14:07 - Samira Patel: for small pass rates use absolute thresholds, for larger baselines percent is fine. mixing both works: e.g. alert if drop >1.5% absolute or >7% relative.
00:14:18 - Carlos Rivera: ok let's pick that for billing prompts.
00:14:21 - 00:14:48 - Speaker 3: (overlap) the team also wants to confirm retrain vs prompt engineering tradeoffs; sometimes small prompt fixes are faster than retraining.
00:14:53 - Samira Patel: yes we prefer iterative prompt fixes first; retrain when you have >1,000 labeled examples or systematic errors. retraining takes longer but can fix systemic bias.
00:15:02 - Maya Chen: how do we measure regressions after retrain? do you replay prior test set?
00:15:06 - Samira Patel: we keep a frozen evaluation suite for regression testing and run a full sweep pre/post retrain. we also compute delta for each prompt and overall metrics.
00:15:17 - Jordan Miller: any blockers for the pilot?
00:15:20 - Carlos Rivera: procurement needs SOC2 and cost numbers, and we need the failing examples uploaded. timeline wise procurement aims to sign pilot by end of month if both are ok.
00:15:31 - Jordan Miller: we'll prioritize the SOC 2 and pricing doc.
00:15:34 - 00:15:58 - Samira Patel: last thing - I started a regression playbook in the eval sheet with triage steps: 1) check sample size, 2) examine context and kv cache, 3) try prompt hardening, 4) apply guardrail patch, 5) consider dedicated variant or retrain. link in chat.
00:16:05 - Maya Chen: that's useful, can you add a column for severity and customer impact?
00:16:09 - Samira Patel: yes will add severity labels (P0/P1/P2) and suggested mitigation.
00:16:15 - Jordan Miller: ok wrapping - summary of next steps: Samira send updated prompt set and YAML for alerts, Jordan send pilot pricing and SOC2, Maya upload failing examples, Ravi create CRM tracker.
00:16:27 - Carlos Rivera: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
00:16:30 - Liam O'Neill: thanks, talk soon.
00:16:33 - Jordan Miller: thanks all, we'll follow up in the doc and set the next call for 07/22.
00:16:40 - Meeting end

Notes on transcription: occasional cut words, speaker overlap, some proper nouns may be mis-transcribed (vendor names), timestamps approximate. Shared artifacts: https://drive.google.com/fin_sight_eval (eval sheet), Redwood_playbook.yaml (alert config)
